records.name: 1791 Delegates
records.summary: A nonprofit with offices in Philadelphia, New York and Washington, DC. It offers online courses on religious literacy and public life, and classroom materials on rights and respect for schools.
records.what_you_do: Take one of its online courses on religious literacy and public life through ReligionAndPublicLife.org. Most of its other projects are curriculum and consulting for schools and other groups, not something a visitor can join directly.

first_step.how: Browse the online course list at ReligionAndPublicLife.org and pick a course that fits your interests.
first_step.basis: The courses are online, but the group's own pages give no sign-up steps, price, or first-visit guidance, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group's own pages describe online courses and certificates but do not say how long a course takes, what it costs, or whether there are live sessions. Check the course page on the learning site before you sign up.

records.notes: The Philadelphia link is an office address only. Its programs are mostly online or national, so a reviewer should decide whether it belongs in the directory. The learning site (ReligionAndPublicLife.org) returned HTTP 403 and was not read, so course cost, length and sign-up steps are unverified. The contact page lists no email, phone or form. The programs page names partner groups that were not checked, including Philadelphia Commons Institute and Interfaith America.

records.name: Philadelphia Area Group Psychotherapy Society
records.summary: A membership society for people who lead therapy groups in the Philadelphia region. Its monthly Consultation Group gives clinicians a place to talk through their group work.
records.what_you_do: Bring your group clinical work to the monthly online Consultation Group, or join the society for member rates and benefits.

schedule.text: Monthly on the second Wednesday, 7:00 to 8:30 pm, online. Sessions run September through May.

cost.text: $15 per monthly session for members and $25 for non-members, as listed on the group's home page.

first_step.how: Use the Reserve Your Spot button on the Consultation Group page (pagps.org/consultation-group) to book a session.
first_step.basis: The session is open to anyone who wants to talk through their clinical group work and has a clear reserve button, but the page gives no first-visit or new-here guidance.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each session runs an hour and a half online, once a month on the second Wednesday evening. The page does not say how a session is run or how many people attend. The fee is $15 for members and $25 for non-members, according to the home page.
first_visit_tips: Reserve your spot ahead of time through the Consultation Group page.
Plan to join online from a device with internet access.

records.notes: Cost wording differs between pages. The Consultation Group page says the fee starts at $15 and does not split member and non-member rates, while the home page gives $15 for members and $25 for non-members. The record uses the home page wording, and the group should confirm. The upcoming events page lists no events at the moment. The join page names the American Group Psychotherapy Association as its parent affiliate; not checked and not added to leads_only. The equity rate applies to event and conference registration, not the Consultation Group. The facilitator's direct email is not recorded; the group's general contact email is used.

records.name: Art City Opera
records.summary: A Philadelphia opera company that stages full productions, many exploring current social issues, and says it offers workshops for early-career singers.
records.what_you_do: Attend one of its staged productions, many of which take on current social issues. Sign up for the newsletter to hear about audition postings and workshops.

schedule.text: Full productions each season, listed on the company's site. Shows are not on a fixed weekly schedule.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not posted on the company's own site, and donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Pick a production from the 2026 to 2027 season list on artcityopera.org and buy a ticket through its ticket link.
first_step.basis: Anyone can attend a show, but the site shows no dates or prices, its ticket link is labeled as a donation, and it does not explain how to audition or join a workshop.
first_step.what_to_expect: A production is a full staged opera that runs about two hours, according to a festival listing for one of the company's shows. The company's own site does not post ticket prices, but that listing showed $35 for general admission with pay-what-you-can seats from $10.
first_visit_tips: The festival listing for one production recommended ages 13 and up and warned about violence, audience interaction, and sexual content, so read the listing for the show you pick.
Some links on the company's site labeled Donate lead to a ticketing page, so check that you are buying a ticket for the show you want.

records.notes: The company's own pages list four 2026 to 2027 productions (Don(na) Giovanni, Alcina, Entartete Musik, Trouble in Tahiti) with no dates or prices. The Don(na) Giovanni dates, venue and price come from a third-party Philadelphia Fringe listing: performances on September 24, 26 and 27, 2026 at the Louis Bluver Theatre at the Drake, 302 S Hicks St. The listing does not name the city. The workshop for early-career singers is named on the homepage only; the projects page does not describe it and a web search found no listing for it. Opera Philadelphia's Emerging Artist Program is in leads_only. The IRS address appeared twice in the old file, so one copy is kept. No opera tag exists, so choir_singing is the closest tag. The contact page uses a form; its email is not recorded.

records.name: Black Women in Sport Foundation
records.summary: A nonprofit that works to get Black women and girls into sport. Its youth program offers after-school sports and academic enrichment for girls, and it gives college scholarships each year.
records.what_you_do: Girls take part in after-school and summer sports such as fencing, tennis, lacrosse, and soccer, at schools and recreation centers. Volunteers can coordinate a local activity, help run a fundraiser, staff an event table, or mentor, tutor, or coach in a program.

schedule.text: After-school programs at Philadelphia schools and recreation centers, with summer programming. Days and times vary by location and are not posted.

cost.text: The site does not state what the youth program costs. Families are asked to contact the group for enrollment details.

first_step.how: Send a message through the Contact Us page on blackwomeninsport.org to ask how to enroll in the youth program.
first_step.basis: Families are asked to contact the group directly to enroll, a clear first step, but the site gives no forms, fees, age ranges, or first-session details.
first_step.what_to_expect: Youth sessions mix sports such as fencing, field hockey, golf, and softball with academic enrichment, and they focus on confidence and healthy habits. The group provides equipment to students. The site does not say how long a session lasts, how many girls attend, or what it costs, so ask when you get in touch.
first_visit_tips: Ask about enrollment steps, forms, and fees through the Contact Us page before the first day.
Ask which school or recreation center a session meets at, since days and times vary by location.

records.notes: The youth page footer reads 2020 and its program details are undated, so confirm current details with the group. The volunteer page lists an email address whose domain looks misspelled, so no email is recorded. The triathlon page describes grant-funded training for 2022 races with 2022 deadlines, so no current triathlon program is shown and none is listed here. Scholarships (four a year for female college students, applications March 1 to 31) are closed right now per the scholarships page. The contact page gives PO Box 2610, Philadelphia, PA 19130 as the mailing address; the IRS street address is kept. Two staff email addresses appear on the contact page and are not recorded.

records.name: Children First Action Fund
records.summary: A Pennsylvania advocacy group that pushes lawmakers to invest in children living with poverty and hardship. It publishes election guides and candidate questionnaire answers so families can see where officials stand.
records.what_you_do: Read the 2026 Election Center and Child Care Voter guide, including candidate answers on child care and family issues. Sign up for updates in the 'Be a Part of the Action' section, and follow the group on Facebook or Instagram.

first_step.how: Sign up for updates in the 'Be a Part of the Action' section of childrenfirstactionfund.org to get updates.
first_step.basis: Open to the public: the guides are free to read and sign-up for updates is clearly marked, though no meetings or volunteer steps are described.
first_step.what_to_expect: There are no meetings or events listed. A first visit means reading the 2026 ballot guide, which covers candidate answers on child care, pre-K, paid leave, and the child care workforce, and using the voter tools to check or register. There is no fee to read the guides, though the site also asks for donations.
first_visit_tips: The Election Center lists Pennsylvania voter deadlines for the November 3, 2026 election, starting with registering by October 19, 2026.
Use the voter tools on the Election Center page to check your registration or find your polling place.

records.notes: The guides and candidate answers show no publication or update dates, so no last-activity month is set. The group describes itself as nonpartisan and the record sets partisan to false on that basis. The sign-up for updates sits on the homepage (#signup) rather than its own page. The Facebook group and Instagram links are social links and were not checked.

records.name: Focused Athletics
records.summary: A nonprofit that supports young athletes with tutoring, college application help, mentoring, and gym training at partner gyms. Volunteers can tutor, coach, or mentor.
records.what_you_do: Athletes train at partner gyms in the Philadelphia area and get academic help, including tutoring, test prep, and college application support, plus mentoring. Volunteers can email the group about tutoring, coaching, or mentoring.

schedule.text: Days, times, and training locations are not stated. Training takes place at local gyms through partnerships.

cost.text: Athletes train at partner gyms free of charge. The site does not state fees for tutoring or test prep.

first_step.how: Use the Sign Up page on focusedathletics.org to register as a student athlete, and sign the participant waiver.
first_step.basis: The site has a sign-up page and a volunteer email, so the way in is clear, but eligibility, tryouts, and start dates are not stated.
first_step.what_to_expect: The sign-up form asks about the athlete's school, sports played, and a parent or guardian contact, and it also asks for some academic details. The page does not say when training starts, how long a session lasts, or how many athletes train together.
first_visit_tips: Have a parent or guardian's name, email, and phone ready for the sign-up form.
Email the group to ask about start dates and training times, since the site does not list them.

records.notes: The homepage lists tutoring, coaching and mentoring volunteer options, but the Get Involved and Tutoring pages do not describe those roles. The record follows the homepage and should be confirmed. The contact page lists a mailing address in Media, PA 19063, outside the city, while the IRS address is on Walnut Street in Philadelphia. A reviewer should confirm the group works in the city. The menu links a Philly Hope Line brochure from Uplift Philly, a different organization; not checked and not added to leads_only because no URL was taken from the page. Eligibility for athletes is not stated.

records.name: Friends of Franklin
records.notes: The group's About Us page says the nonprofit, formed in 1983, stopped its paid-member newsletter in 2013 and dissolved its corporation. The website is now a personal Franklin blog run by one person. It still posts (newest post July 2026) and hosts the Gazette archive, but the organization itself is closed, so the record is hidden as defunct. The blog owner's personal contact details were not recorded. The Subscribe page is a blog email list, not a membership.

leads_only.note: Named in a web search for early-career singer programs in Philadelphia; not checked, and the 2026 to 2027 class is not confirmed.

notes: Seven groups read from data/groups and deep-fetched. Friends of Franklin moved to hide (defunct): its About Us page says the corporation dissolved in 2013, and the blog that remains is one person's. 1791 Delegates' course site returned HTTP 403, so its course cost and sign-up steps are unverified and confidence stays low. Art City Opera's Don(na) Giovanni dates, venue and ticket price come from a third-party Philadelphia Fringe listing, cited in sources; the company's own site shows none. Three groups reached the six-fetch cap (PAGPS, Art City Opera, Black Women in Sport). One WebSearch used of one. No rate limiting seen. Open conflicts are in each record's notes: PAGPS fee wording, Focused Athletics volunteer roles and its Media, PA mailing address, and the Black Women in Sport email domain.
